1.1Prerequisites & Installationcrates.io

Zero Node.js dependency. Pure native Rust.

Yav is engineered to free full-stack web engineering from fragile JavaScript toolchains, npm cascades, and heavy hydration runtimes. All you need is standard Rust (1.75+).

Required Prerequisite

Rust stable (1.75+) installed via rustup.rs.

Eliminated Dependencies

No Node.js, no npm, no pnpm, no webpack, no vite.

bash — yav-cli install
# 1. Install the standalone CLI binary onto your PATH from crates.io
$ cargo install yav-cli
# Or install cutting-edge release directly from GitHub main
$ cargo install --git https://github.com/isaacvay/yav.rs yav-cli
# Verify installation and upgrade project toolchain at any time
$ yav update
1.2Quickstart & High-Velocity Dev Serveryav dev

From zero to running server in 60 seconds.

The Yav CLI automates everything: project scaffolding, automated standalone Tailwind JIT provisioning, live incremental compilation, and WebSocket hot reloading without touching Node.js.

zsh — yav new & dev
# 1. Scaffold a fresh Yav project with file routing and Tailwind CSS
$ yav new my-app
# 2. Enter workspace directory
$ cd my-app
# 3. Start high-velocity dev server with live reload on http://127.0.0.1:3000
$ yav dev
✔ Compiled Tailwind CSS · Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000
Glassmorphism Live Compiler Error Overlay

When a syntax mistake or mismatched Rust type occurs during development, the dev server captures rustc compiler diagnostics and immediately projects an interactive dark-mode error overlay directly onto your browser page, recovering automatically the millisecond you save the fix.

2.1RSX Macro & Markup Syntaxrsx!

JSX ergonomics. Direct buffer streaming.

The rsx! procedural macro translates declarative tags directly into zero-allocation buffer append instructions at build time. There is no Virtual DOM diffing, no synthetic event layer, and zero runtime template parsing overhead.

src/components/ProjectCard.rs

use yav::prelude::*;
#[component]
pub fn ProjectCard(title: &str, stars: u32, is_featured: bool, tags: &[&str]) -> Node {
rsx! {
<div class="p-6 border rounded-lg bg-surface" class:border-oxide={is_featured}>
<h3 class="text-xl font-bold">{title}</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-dim">Stars: {stars}</p>
// Native if/else without closure brackets
if is_featured {
<span class="badge text-ok">Featured</span>
} else {
<span class="badge text-dim">Community</span>
}
// Native for loop directly in RSX
<div class="flex gap-2 mt-3">
for tag in tags.iter() {
<span class="chip text-xs">{*tag}</span>
}
</div>
</div>
}
}
Rust · UTF-8 · ProjectCard.rsCompiled without runtime overhead
Automatic XSS Escaping

Dynamic text and attributes are escaped automatically (&, <, >, ", '). Only explicit Node::raw() bypasses escaping.

No Quotes for Text

Just like in JSX, plain textual content does not require quotes: <p>Welcome to Yav</p> is valid RSX.

Fragments & Nesting

Group sibling nodes without introducing superfluous wrapper elements via empty fragments: <> ... </>.

2.2Component Patterns: Functional & Props Structs#[component]

Two idiomatic patterns for maximum ergonomics.

Yav supports both auto-generated multi-argument props for everyday components and explicit typed structs for complex enterprise interfaces.

Pattern A: Auto Props
UserBadge.rs

#[component]
pub fn UserBadge(
name: String,
is_admin: bool,

<UserBadge name="Alice" is_admin=true />

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct StatCardProps {
pub title: String,
pub value: u64,
pub trend: Option&lt;f32&gt;,

#[component]
pub fn StatCard(props: StatCardProps) -> Node {
rsx! { <div class="plate p-4"><h3>{props.title}</h3></div> }
}

2.5Static Subtree Folding & Zero-Allocation BuffersNode::Static

Compile-time immutable subtree folding.

Unlike typical SSR engines that recursively allocate Node trees on every single HTTP request, the rsx! proc-macro identifies immutable subtrees at compile-time and folds them into Node::Static(&'static str). These branches bypass attribute serialization and write directly to contiguous buffer pools.

crates/yav-core/src/node.rs
Zero Allocations
// Core zero-allocation enum with Cow<'static, str> slices
pub enum Node {
Element(Element),
Text(Cow&lt;'static, str&gt;),
Static(&'static str), // Folded at compile-time, zero heap allocation
Raw(String),
Fragment(Vec&lt;Node&gt;),
}
Zero heap overhead for static markup97% Bare-Metal Throughput
2.6Native Control Flow in RSXif / else & for

Write standard Rust loops directly inside RSX.

In Yav v0.1.5, you write standard Rust control flow directly inside rsx! without needing closure wrappers or .iter().map(...) boilerplate. Short boolean attributes and class directives (class:active={is_active}) are evaluated at compile time.

src/components/UserList.rs
Zero Closure Overhead
// Direct Rust control flow inside rsx! without closure hacks
rsx! {
&lt;div class="user-roster"&gt;
if is_admin {
&lt;span class="badge admin"&gt;"Admin Access"&lt;/span&gt;
} else {
&lt;span class="badge member"&gt;"Member Access"&lt;/span&gt;
}
&lt;ul class="team-list"&gt;
for member in team.iter() {
&lt;li class:leader={member.is_lead}&gt;{*member.name}&lt;/li&gt;
}
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;
}
Transforms into straight buffer appends during compilationNo closure allocation
3.1File-System Routing & Radix Treesauto_routes!

The directory structure is the router.

The auto_routes!(app) macro inspects your src/routes/ directory at compile time, discovers all page handlers, and compiles them into constant-time O(k) Radix routing trees via matchit.

File PathPatternHTTP Method & PathParameter Extractor
src/routes/index.rsRoot IndexGET /—
src/routes/about.rsStatic EndpointGET /about—
src/routes/users/_id_.rsDynamic parameterGET /users/{id}Path(id): Path<u64>
src/routes/docs/__slug__.rsCatch-all wildcardGET /docs/{*slug}Path(slug): Path<String>
src/routes/(auth)/login.rsRoute groupingGET /login— (folder excluded from URL)
src/routes/api/health.rsREST APIGET /api/healthJson<HealthResponse>

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result&lt;(), Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error&gt;&gt; {

3.4Cryptographic Sessions & Signed Flash CookiesHMAC-SHA256

Tamper-proof stateless cookies with constant-time verification.

Sessions and one-time notifications in Yav are cryptographically signed using HMAC-SHA256. Signatures are verified in constant time to eliminate timing side-channel attacks.

use yav::server::{HtmlPage, Session, Flash};
pub async fn dashboard(session: Session, flash: Flash) -> Result&lt;HtmlPage, StatusCode&gt; {
let user = session.get::&lt;User&gt;("user")
.ok_or(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)?;
Ok(HtmlPage::new(rsx! {
<AppLayout>
{if let Some(msg) = flash.get() {
rsx! { <div class="alert-box alert-ok">{msg}</div> }
}}
<h2>Welcome back, {user.name}</h2>
</AppLayout>
})))
}
constant_time_eq verification · HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure5-min Flash TTL
Cookie Injection Hardening

Cookie names, paths, and domains are sanitized against CRLF injection (; \r \n \0), and payloads > 4 KB are discarded before HMAC processing.

Flash Replay Prevention

Flash messages embed signed 5-minute timestamps (DEFAULT_FLASH_TTL_SECS = 300) preventing replay attacks across browser restarts.

3.5CSRF Protection & Sliding-Window Rate Limitingsecurity

Architectural defense against brute force and forgery.

Yav provides built-in cryptographic CSRF token generation and sliding-window rate limiting to protect endpoints against automated bots and cross-site request attacks.

use yav::server::{CsrfToken, FormData, Session, YavError};
// 1. GET handler: bind cryptographic CSRF token to user session
pub async fn login_form(session: Session) -> HtmlPage {
let csrf = CsrfToken::from_session(&session);
HtmlPage::new(rsx! {
<form method="POST" action="/login">
{csrf.hidden_input()}
<input name="email" type="email" required />
<button type="submit">Log In</button>
</form>
})
}
// 2. POST handler: constant-time token verification
pub async fn login_action(session: Session, form: FormData) -> Response {
let csrf = CsrfToken::from_session(&session);
if !csrf.verify(&form) {
return YavError::Forbidden("Invalid CSRF token".into()).into_response();
}
redirect("/dashboard")
}
CsrfToken::verify(&form) constant-time checkProtected
3.6In-Memory SSR Route Caching & Blake3 ETagsget_cached

Sub-millisecond responses without template re-execution.

For dynamic content under high load, get_cached caches rendered HTML in memory. When incoming requests include If-None-Match, Yav computes Blake3/SHA-256 ETags and returns 304 Not Modified instantly, saving CPU and network bandwidth.

src/main.rs
In-Memory Cache
// Cache route HTML for 120 seconds with automatic ETag generation
let app = YavApp::new()
.etag(true) // Enables Blake3 / SHA-256 ETags globally
.get_cached("/blog", Duration::from_secs(120), blog_index_handler)
.static_dir("public");
Bypasses template rendering & database queries304 Not Modified Fast-Path
3.7View Transitions API & Type-Safe Reverse Routingurl_for!

SPA fluid transitions with SSR initial load speed.

Yav's <Link /> component automatically prefetches target pages in the background and morphs views using the native browser View Transitions API (document.startViewTransition), while url_for! ensures type-safe reverse routing without hardcoded URL strings.

Link with Prefetch
View Transitions
// Prefetches on hover, morphs with View Transitions
use yav::ui::Link;
rsx! {
<Link href="/catalogue" prefetch=true>
"Explorer les composants"
</Link>
}
Reverse Routing
url_for!
// Interpolate typed route parameters safely
use yav::router::url_for;
let user_url = url_for(
"/users/:id",
&[("id", "42")],
);
assert_eq!(user_url, "/users/42");
3.8Typed Form Validation & Asset HardeningFromFormData

Typed validation traits and strict path containment.

Parse and validate multipart and URL-encoded forms with the FromFormData trait, while static file serving verifies canonical paths and serves SVGs with strict Content-Security-Policy headers.

src/forms.rs
FromFormData
// Typed form validation with error aggregation
impl FromFormData for RegisterForm {
fn from_form(form: &FormData) -> Result&lt;Self, FormErrors&gt; {
let mut errors = FormErrors::new();
errors.require("email", form.get_or_empty("email"), "Email is required");
if errors.has_errors() { Err(errors) } else { Ok(Self { ... }) }
}
}
Strict canonicalization against directory traversalSVG CSP Sandbox Protection
3.9Native AI SDK, Streaming UI & MCP ServerMcpServer & RAG

Built-in Model Context Protocol & Streaming UI.

Yav includes a native AI runtime: multi-turn Conversation, JSON-Schema ToolRegistry, streaming HTML fragments over SSE (stream_ui_fragment), dense cosine VectorIndex with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), and a full Model Context Protocol (McpServer) endpoint exposing live application tools and prompt resources to Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Copilot.

Model Context Protocol (MCP)
JSON-RPC 2.0
// Expose application tools to AI agents via MCP
use yav::server::mcp::{McpServer, McpTool};
let server = McpServer::new("yav-backend", "1.0")
.tool(McpTool::new("query_db")
.description("Executes read-only SQL queries")
.handler(handle_sql_tool))
.resource("schema://postgres", db_schema);
// Mounts at POST /_yav/mcp
app.mount_mcp(server);
Streaming UI Fragments
SSE Stream
// Stream AI-generated RSX fragments progressively
use yav::server::ai::stream_ui_fragment;
pub async fn ai_agent(req: Request) -&gt; SseStream {
stream_ui_fragment(req, |chunk| {
rsx! { "&lt;p class='ai-token'&gt;" {chunk} "&lt;/p&gt;" }
}).await
}
3.10Proactive Resilience & Distributed CoordinationCircuitBreaker & XFetch

Zero cascading failures. Automatic fail-safe.

Built for mission-critical enterprise environments: CircuitBreaker isolates struggling microservices, Bulkhead limits concurrent execution slots, TransactionalOutbox guarantees dual-write consistency, DbReplicaPool steers reads to geographic replicas with read-your-own-writes session stickiness, and DistributedCache mitigates stampedes via the probabilistic XFetch algorithm.

src/resilience.rs
CircuitBreaker & XFetch
// Proactive resilience protecting downstream services
use yav::server::resilience::{CircuitBreaker, Bulkhead};
use yav::server::distributed_cache::{DistributedCache, MemoryL1Store};
let cb = CircuitBreaker::builder("payment-api")
.failure_threshold(5)
.recovery_timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
.build();
// XFetch: probabilistic early recomputation eliminates cache stampedes
let cache = DistributedCache::new(MemoryL1Store::new(), redis_pool)
.xfetch_beta(1.2); // probabilistic delta evaluation
Protects DB connection pools and API rate limits from collapseXFetch Stampede Elimination
3.11Passkeys / WebAuthn & ReBAC Zanzibar AuthorizationFIDO2 & Zanzibar

Passwordless biometric auth and graph authorization.

Native passwordless FIDO2 authentication via PasskeyManager supporting Apple Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello, and YubiKeys without external cloud auth vendors. For permissions, RebacGraph delivers Google Zanzibar-style relationship-based access control with transitive resolution and cycle-safe graph traversals.

PasskeyManager (FIDO2)
WebAuthn Native
// Challenge generation & biometric signature validation
use yav::server::passkeys::PasskeyManager;
let pm = PasskeyManager::new("yav.rs", "https://yav.rs");
let challenge = pm.generate_register_challenge(user_id);
let credential = pm.verify_register(user_id, response)?;
ReBAC Zanzibar Graph
Relationship-Based
// Fine-grained graph authorization with transitive roles
use yav::server::rebac::RebacGraph;
let mut graph = RebacGraph::new();
graph.add_relation("doc:42", "editor", "user:alice");
graph.add_relation("doc:42", "viewer", "team:frontend");
assert!(graph.check("user:bob", "viewer", "doc:42"));
3.12GraphQL, TurboStream, Event Sourcing & Tus UploadsModern Protocols

All open standards natively implemented in pure Rust.

Connect any client architecture with zero external proxy dependencies: zero-dependency GraphQlSchema with embedded GraphiQL 3.x playground, TurboStream 7-action multi-zone DOM mutation streaming, EventStore CQRS aggregates with optimistic concurrency, and resumable file uploads conforming to the open Tus Protocol v1.0.0 with disk spooling protection against out-of-memory denial of service.

src/protocols.rs
Tus v1.0.0 & TurboStream
// Hotwire TurboStream multi-zone mutation & Tus resumable uploads
use yav::server::turbo_stream::{TurboStream, TurboAction};
use yav::server::resumable_upload::ChunkedUploader;
// 1. Stream HTML fragment targeting container ID without full reload
let mutation = TurboStream::new(TurboAction::Prepend, "messages", "&lt;div class='msg'&gt;New alert&lt;/div&gt;");
// 2. Resumable chunked file upload with disk spooling
let uploader = ChunkedUploader::new("uploads/").max_file_size(10 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024);
Full RFC compliance with pure Rust memory safetyZero Node.js / Zero C Libraries

4.2Cursor Tracking & Reactive 3D Effectsyav:cursor

Hardware-accelerated mouse coordinates & 3D perspective.

The cursor runtime (~1.3 KB) tracks pointer position using passive requestAnimationFrame loops and publishes high-precision reactive CSS variables onto elements: --yav-mouse-x, --yav-mouse-y, and normalized coordinates.

4.3Spring Physics & WAAPI Motion EnginesolveSpring

Mechanical mass, stiffness, and damping physics.

Motion in Yav is defined using physical harmonic oscillator equations (stiffness, damping, mass) solved into exact analytical sine/cosine curves and fed directly to Element.animate(). Initial states are pre-compiled into inline CSS during SSR for guaranteed zero-FOUC.

src/components/MotionShowcase.rs
< 1.8 KB WAAPI Runtime
// 1. Declarative motion element with hover and tap recoils
<div yav:initial="opacity:0, y:24, scale:0.95" yav:animate="opacity:1, y:0, scale:1" yav:spring="320, 18, 1" yav:hover="scale:1.02, y:-4">
"Card content animated with spring physics"
</div>
// 2. Specialized UI Motion Components
use yav::ui::{CountUp, AnimatedBar, TypewriterCode};
<CountUp to={124500.0} prefix="+" suffix=" req/s" duration_ms={1400} />
<AnimatedBar target_pct={97.4} duration_ms={1200} />
<TypewriterCode speed_ms={14} skip_on_click=true>
<div>"pub fn main() { println!(\"Fast\"); }"</div>
</TypewriterCode>

<div class="track h-2 bg-zinc-800 rounded mt-4">

</div>

4.6SSR Tree-Shaking Runtimes & WebSockets0 KB JS Guarantee

Only pay for what your page actually renders.

During HTML serialization, Yav scans the rendered DOM string and tree-shakes client runtimes before transmitting the response. If a page uses no interactive attributes, exactly 0 bytes of client JavaScript are injected. For real-time updates, WsBroadcast pushes server-rendered HTML fragments over WebSockets.

Detected Attributes on PageInjected Micro-RuntimeBundle Overhead
yav:toggle, yav:copy, yav:hotkey, yav:tab, yav:filteryav-micro-actions~2.1 KB
yav:cursor, CursorSpotlight, TiltPlate, Magneticyav-cursor-runtime~1.3 KB
yav:animate, CountUp, AnimatedBar, TypewriterCodeyav-motion-runtime~1.8 KB
yav:state, yav:bind, yav:text, yav:on-clickyav-signals-runtime~0.9 KB
None of the above (Static Page)None0 KB JS

5.1Asset Pipeline & In-Memory Pre-Compressionbrotli + gzip

Blake3 ETags and zero on-the-fly CPU compression tax.

During yav build, static assets are fingerprinted (styles.[hash].css) and pre-compressed into Brotli (.br) and Gzip (.gz) archives in a single in-memory pass. The server streams pre-compressed buffers directly from memory matching the client's Accept-Encoding header.

Blake3 ETags & 304 Not Modified

All assets calculate ultra-fast Blake3 hashes. Repeat client visits receive 304 headers in microseconds without redundant byte transmissions.

Strict Path Traversal Hardening

Relative path escapes (../) and null bytes are rejected at the kernel interface; canonical paths are bounded strictly within public/.

5.2Static Site Generation (SSG with yav export)yav export

Pre-render all routes to static HTML for zero-server hosting.

If your project consists of documentation, marketing pages, or blogs, yav export crawls and renders all discovered static routes into standalone HTML files ready to deploy on Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Netlify, or AWS S3.

SSG EXPORTyav export
# Export all discovered static routes into dist/ directory
$ yav export
# Specify custom output path and production base URL for canonical tags
$ yav export --output dist --base-url https://mon-site.com
Generates directory-structured index.html filesZero-Server Static Output

5.6Database Migrations & SQL Scaffolding (yav db)yav db

Deterministic SQL migrations with SHA-256 cryptographic journaling.

The yav db command provides an integrated migration runner for SQLite and PostgreSQL. It reads your database URL from .env, applies forward migrations, enables one-command rollbacks, and verifies SHA-256 checksums in the _yav_migrations journal to prevent migration drift across environments.

DATABASE WORKFLOWyav db
# 1. Initialize migrations directory and configure DATABASE_URL in .env
$ yav db init
# 2. Create a timestamped SQL migration with UP and DOWN sections
$ yav db new create_users_table
# 3. Execute all pending migrations and commit SHA-256 hashes to journal
$ yav db migrate
# 4. Check migration status, history, and checksum integrity
$ yav db status
# 5. Rollback the most recent migration step
$ yav db rollback
Native SQLite & PostgreSQL runnersSHA-256 Journaled
